messages:
Kai: Heads-up — after last runtime deploy (v1.14.0) + the q4_k_m model conversion we pushed yesterday, prefix cache hit-rate on stable-prod dropped from ~82% -> ~27% for the conversational endpoint. Latency P50 for short prompts jumped ~40ms.

Raj: Yikes. Did we change cache keying or the KV layout in the runtime?

Kai: I dug into traces. Looks like kernel selection changed attention fusion kernel (ATTN_FUSE_v2) which alters the in-memory KV layout. Our cache key generation is still serializing raw KV bytes + model_name. That means identical token-prefixes produce different keys if the kernel stores KV differently.

Amanda: Can you paste the logs showing mismatch?

Kai: Sure — snippet from request traces (before vs after):

```
# before (v1.13.7)
prefix_tokens=[101,102,103]
prefix_key_hash=0x7a3c1f
kv_layout=layout=separate(k,v)
cache_lookup: HIT -> served from prefix_cache

# after (v1.14.0 + ATTN_FUSE_v2)
prefix_tokens=[101,102,103]
prefix_key_hash=0xd2b8e4
kv_layout=layout=interleaved(kv)
cache_lookup: MISS -> full compute
```

Raj: That matches my suspicion. We used raw tensor bytes hashing as a quick path. If layout changes, hashes change.

Marco: Perf-bot reports: cache_hits=12, cache_misses=31, hit_rate=27%, measured over last 10m for conv-prod. Overall tokens/sec increased cost ~35%.

Perf-bot: <automated> profile: endpoint: /v1/chat/stream; p50_latency: 112ms (+40ms); p95_latency: 238ms; tokens_served: 1.2M; cache_hit_rate: 0.27.

Sylvia: Is this only for q4_k_m variants or across all quant profiles?

Kai: Mostly q4_k_m + any model variant where the runtime picked the fused attention kernel. Non-fused kernels still match old layout so those keep hits.

Amanda: Two-pronged fix: short-term warmup/backfill so customers aren't affected; long-term fix to keying so layout changes don't break cache.

Raj: Proposed permanent fix: compute prefix cache key from canonicalized metadata: (model_name, model_variant_tag, tokenizer_hash, token_ids_sequence) and NOT from serialized KV bytes. Then include a kernel_version tag in the cache metadata so we can invalidate gracefully on incompatible kernel upgrades.

Kai: Agreed. Also add a compatibility flag: if runtime sees a key with older kernel_version, allow a fast reserialize->normalize path to convert into canonical key during lookup (cheap for small prefixes).

Marco: For immediate mitigation: run a priming job that replays top-5k prefix token sequences per model variant (based on last 7d traffic) to repopulate the cache under v1.14.0 layout. This will cost some transient GPU cycles but should restore hit-rate quickly.

Amanda: I'll kick off a priming job. Plan: steam the top 5k prefixes for each high-traffic model variant, 2 workers per region, rate-limit to avoid thrashing. Target: 2 hours run.

Raj: I'll open a PR for the keying change. ETA: afternoon patch + tests. The hash function change is backwards-compatible if we keep kernel_version in metadata.

Sylvia: We should also add automated checks in CI that assert cache_key stability for stable kernels. When we change kernel layouts we need a controlled migration plan.

Kai: Good call. Add a unit test that takes token_ids -> expected canonical_key (golden file) and fails if key changes unless kernel bump is explicitly allowed.

Infra-bot: <automated> Created ticket RW-8723: "prefix-cache: canonical keying + migration plan" assigned to Raj.

Amanda: Priming job started. Monitoring dashboards updated (temp backfill job).

Marco: Early signs: hit-rate creeping back to ~64% after 22 minutes of priming for q4_k_m variant in us-east-1. Latency moving down.

Raj: PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/529 — implements token-id-based keying and kernel_version metadata. Includes conversion utility and unit tests.

Kai: After merging, we should run a staged rollout: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% and run a backfill window in parallel to avoid cold starts for new keys.

Sylvia: Also add instrumentation: metric prefix_cache_mismatch_reasons with labels {reason=[kv_layout,missing_meta,tokenizer_mismatch]} so we can triage future drops quickly.

Amanda: Will follow up with postmortem note in #postmortems after we see final numbers. For now: monitoring + priming + keying PR in flight.

Marco: Owners: Raj = keying PR + tests; Amanda = priming job + monitor; Kai = rollout plan + metrics; Sylvia = CI gating + postmortem write-up.

Kai: Thanks everyone. Lesson: never hash raw runtime-internal bytes for stable cache keys.

Raj: on it. will update the thread with PR link and canary results. :thumbsup:
